Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the low tail latency on long-running queries. We're getting internal buy-in to add Redwood's observability suite (retention extension, distributed tracing, and the new advanced dashboards) into our production plan but need a few pricing/packaging clarifications before procurement will greenlight an order. High level:

- Target retention: 13 months for logs/metrics (estimated 2.5 TB compressed/month)
- Tracing: ~1.2M traces/month, 30% sampling is acceptable if it meaningfully reduces cost
- Dashboards: advanced widgets, 8 editors, 30 viewers

Questions:
1) Do you offer a modular bundle vs per-feature pricing? We prefer a predictable ARR but want the option to scale features independently.
2) Any pilot / ramp pricing for first 90 days?
3) What discount bands exist at $120k-$200k ARR?
4) Procurement needs a provisional quote & attachment list so they can start the PO process.

Could you send a short options matrix (SKU-level) and an initial quote? If we can get to a 12-month commitment with a ~15% discount we'll proceed quickly.

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear summary and the requirements doc. Quick responses up front, then a couple of concrete options attached.

Short answers:
- Yes — we support both modular (line-item SKUs) and a bundled "Visibility Suite" that combines retention + tracing + advanced dashboards at a discounted ARR.
- Pilot: we recommend a 90-day pilot at 30% of the annualized price (applied as a credit on the first invoice) — common for customers this size.
- Discount bands: 10% at ~$75k ARR, 15% at $125k ARR, 20% at $200k+ ARR (these are our standard public bands; we can negotiate add-ons/credits).

Attached is a provisional quote with three options (A/B/C):
A) Modular (pay-as-you-grow): retention @ $0.045/GB-month, tracing @ $12 per 100k traces, dashboards seats (editor/viewer) per-seat. No term discount.
B) Visibility Suite (12mo commit): flat ARR $138,000/year — includes 13-month retention tier for up to 2.8 TB/mo ingest, 1.2M traces with 30% sampling profile, 8 editors + 30 viewers, and 10 hours enablement. Includes a 15% volume discount applied to tokenized ingest charges.
C) Enterprise (24mo commit): $165,000/year — adds higher SLA (99.95% access), 20% discount across add-ons, 40 hours enablement, plus one training day.

Pilot path: we can put them on option B for a 90-day pilot billed at 30% of the pro-rated annual fee and convert to the annual invoice on signature.

I've attached the provisional PDF quote (Redwood-provisional-quote-DF-0093.pdf). If procurement wants line-item SKUs for the PO, we can expand B into explicit SKUs.

Notes for procurement: retention is metered by compressed GB-month; tracing by sampled traces ingested; dashboards by seat type. If DataFlux expects a different sampling plan or higher retention, costs will scale accordingly.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the quote.

Thanks,

Olga / Marcus — quick internal notes before we reply to Amelia:

- Customer target ARR range (120k–200k) maps to our 15–20% band. If they can commit 24 months, push for 20% + 1 training day + 8 additional enablement hours.
- Tradeoff idea: propose retention tier of 9 months as a lower-cost baseline with an add-on clause to enable 13 months at a delta price. Many customers accept a lower default retention for a step increase.
- SLA: they asked for 99.9 access. 99.95 is in option C; consider offering 99.9 in B at no increase to hit their procurement ask.
- Pilot: accept the 30% pilot credit but require a conversion clause (signed order within 120 days or pilot fees convert to pay-as-you-go).

I also recommend we add a small concession: an onboarding credit of $6,000 if they sign within 30 days. That helps move procurement.

I'll prepare an updated option B that: (a) includes a 15% list, (b) offers 99.9 SLA, (c) adds the $6k onboarding credit, and (d) makes the retention delta explicit.

Karthik
